settingText: PRESENT — approach to the Core-Forge, the place Adrian says the Reset was enacted. Modern construction occupies ancient foundations that are increasingly visible through one another.
summary: Theo, Rae and Adrian reach the site where the forgotten war was erased from lived continuity. Present architecture no longer fully hides the ancient place beneath it. Adrian intends to repeat the Reset if the public memory crisis continues widening.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Theo, Rae and Adrian approach the Core-Forge through ordinary modern construction laid over ancient foundations. Some walls align impossibly with older ones, but the characters remain visually dominant.
Panel 2 — Theo steps ahead of Rae and blocks Adrian's path deeper into the chamber: 'You brought us here to do it again.' Adrian stops at the threshold with both hands visible and empty.
Panel 3 — Adrian: 'I brought you here because I don't know what else stops this.' His back stays against the doorway, shoulders tight and face pale; he does not move toward the central scar.
Panel 4 — Rae: 'Not knowing should terrify you.' Adrian: 'It does.' No one touches a console, studies a schematic or explains how the Reset works.

Panel 5 — Wide threshold panel. Rae stands centered a step ahead of Theo and Adrian; all three face the same scarred chamber entrance but keep visible distance from one another. Old dark masonry and newer construction meet around the doorway.

settingText: PAST — outside the final council, Kyn and Afterlight share a quiet moment while the others continue arguing behind the door.
summary: Kyn asks Afterlight whether people can recover if the war ends. Afterlight says recovery is possible only if they stop demanding that recovery restore what was lost. Their exchange gives the Reset debate a human alternative to victory.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Outside the council door. Kyn and Afterlight sit somewhere unceremonious while muffled argument continues behind them. Let exhaustion soften faction distinctions. Kyn: 'If it stopped tonight, could they heal?' Afterlight answers, 'Some.'

Panel 2 — Kyn: 'That's all?' Afterlight: 'That's always all.' They sit close beside the same exhausted survivor; Kyn's hand remains under the survivor's while Afterlight keeps one hand on the repaired ground.
Panel 3 — Kyn: 'I keep wanting more than that.' Afterlight looks at Kyn, then at her own tired hands. Kyn follows the gaze and their shoulders settle into the same exhausted posture.

Panel 4 — Afterlight: 'So do I. That's how we hurt people.' End almost tenderly, with two people from opposing philosophies admitting that demanding complete repair can become another form of violence.

dialogueInline.text: If it stopped tonight, could they heal?

settingText: PRESENT — intercut ordinary locations after the Core-Forge choice: Olyria-Prime worksite, Zenith archives, Tyrellis transit platform, Neo-Vectra civic route, then the Core-Forge exit.
summary: Nothing resolves cleanly, but the consequence is shown through people already known: Vark protects workers rather than reporting impossible recollections, Caelum leaves returning records visible, the Tyrellis worker's partner stays with him, and the Neo-Vectra couple crosses the reopened route together. The trio accepts that memory and conflict must now be handled socially rather than universally controlled.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Olyria-Prime shift room. Vark listens while one worker insists they remember a corridor that does not exist and another remembers nothing. Vark quietly closes an incident form before anyone can turn the contradiction into a disciplinary report, then pushes the coffee pot toward them. Ordinary shift noise continues.

Panel 2 — Zenith archives. Caelum stands beside a junior archivist as another erased record repopulates. Instead of removing it, he moves his hand away from the delete control and leaves the entry visible. Around them clerks keep working, visibly uncertain about the new policy.

Panel 3 — Tyrellis transit platform. The same TRANSIT WORKER from Issue 6 sits with the same PARTNER; the worker is still grieving the impossible brother while the partner covers both work radios and stays beside him. Trains keep arriving.

Panel 4 — Neo-Vectra. The recurring MAN and WOMAN from Issue 7 walk through the reopened route together carrying the same bags and keys. Behind them, officials replace recovered-affiliation barriers with ordinary behavior-based security and open access.

Panel 5 — Back at the Core-Forge exit. Theo looks at the unchanged scar chamber behind them: 'So what happens now?' Rae is already walking toward the voices outside: 'People remember what they remember.'

Panel 6 — Adrian: 'And if it starts the war again?' Rae: 'Then we stop the war.' Adrian: 'That's not the same thing.' Rae: 'Exactly.' End on the trio joining the occupied corridor rather than standing alone in the chamber.

dialogueInline.text: And if it starts the war again?

settingText: PRESENT — deep-space observation window after the immediate crisis, Theo, Rae and Adrian looking out at a familiar sky.
summary: The trio sees that a familiar region of the night sky is simply wrong: stars everyone remembers are absent. Nobody can tell whether they were erased, belonged only to replacement history, or were lost when continuity returned. Reality's memory has consequences beyond personal recollection.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Quiet observation window after the immediate crisis. Theo, Rae and Adrian look at a familiar region of deep space. No alarms or instruments announce the problem. Theo points through the observation window: 'Were those always gone?' A familiar star cluster has a clean dark gap where several stars should be; render it as ordinary black sky with missing points of light and no glow or distortion.

Panel 2 — Rae: 'No.' She steps close to the glass and fixes on the dark gap, face still and certain; Adrian watches Rae instead of the sky. Adrian: 'I don't know.' Give the admission room; for once he does not hide uncertainty behind protection or authority. Theo: 'You finally said it.' Adrian: 'Get used to hearing it.'

Panel 3 — Final wide panel: three small people facing a sky with a meaningful absence. Truth has returned unevenly; certainty has diminished. Do not reveal Flux, Regent or a technical explanation for the missing stars.
